database.title: Pick a database
database.undo: Switching databases later means moving every saved record.

reasons.rel: your users share data with each other
reasons.ops: nobody wants to run a database server
reasons.host: it runs on your host as is
reasons.cost: it stays cheap at your size

questions.t: Will people share things with each other in the app?
questions.why: Shared data needs records that point at each other.

a.l: No, each person keeps their own

questions.t: Who will keep the database running?
questions.why: Someone has to patch it, back it up, and watch it.

questions.t: How many users do you expect in the first year?
questions.why: Sets how much cost and room to grow matter.
Some hosts don't keep files, which rules out a database file.
alt: hosting moved to a server you run

a.l: A serverless host, like Vercel or Netlify
A server you run, like a VM or container

pg.sub: Postgres hosted for you, for example on Neon
pg.use: Install `pg` and connect with a DATABASE_URL from a managed Postgres provider such as Neon.
good: Sharing is ordinary linked records with simple queries.
The provider handles backups and patches.
bad: Adds a vendor account, and local development needs a connection string.
A monthly bill once you pass the free tier.

turso.sub: SQLite over the network, for example on Turso
turso.use: Install `@libsql/client` and connect with the hosted database URL and token.
good: The same SQLite engine locally and in production.
Low cost while you are small.
bad: Fewer hosting integrations and tools support it.
A smaller ecosystem if you need extensions later.

mongo.sub: MongoDB hosted for you, for example on Atlas
mongo.use: Install `mongoose` and connect with a MongoDB Atlas connection string.
good: Record shapes can change without migrations.
Spreads across machines when collections get large.
bad: Sharing between users needs manual references and extra queries.
Reports across users get harder to write.

sqlite.sub: One database file next to the app

ko.why: Serverless hosts don't keep files between requests, so saved data would vanish.

sqlite.use: Install `better-sqlite3` and keep the database file on the server's disk.
good: Free, one file, nothing to sign up for.
bad: Only works where the disk is kept.
One machine only; growing means a migration.
